rites.name: Crasten
rites.text: Crasten is a bioengineered tide of mutated dwellers in the sealed warrens of Fenernareld, shaped by a clandestine program that wrapped captured subjects in a drifting luminous mist until their bodies swelled and their minds guttered. They lumber through the underways in packs, mostly mindless, but their hunger for the glow makes them a constant hazard to anyone who strays too close.

rites.name: Sileiniel
rites.text: Sileiniel is a concept of the Fenernareld, the thread of stillness that the old tellers say held the Shards together after the Sundering. It is remembered in the Fall as a quiet that outlasted the breaking, and in the Pact as the vow that kept the broken worlds from falling further apart.

rites.name: Drakaiktun
rites.text: Drakaiktun is a concept of the Fenernareld cycle, named for the drake-banner orders that raised the first holding walls in the Walled Age. During the Age of Sundering its doctrine taught that landfall breaks old oaths, so its adherents bound themselves to stone rather than to kin.

rites.name: Tiles
rites.text: A deliberate method of broadcasting messages that shape how a crowd feels and what it believes. Rival camps on a war-torn world use it to rally their people, and some speakers use it to argue against fighting.

rites.name: Crudornath
rites.text: Crudornath is a brutal close-quarters strike from the Grounded realm's E6 era, delivered by a fist wrapped in cracked iron plates that stuns a foe before the blow lands. Opponents who fail to read its sideways lunge rarely escape, though its wind-up is loud enough that veterans can sidestep it.

rites.name: Thoreld
rites.text: Thoreld is a sealed, quiet event of the Grounded realm, a single afternoon of pale rain that falls for exactly one hour across the cliffside villages of Fenernareld. Its strange power is that anyone who hears the rain stop will remember a name they never learned. Those who gather to wait for it sometimes find the names of the dead written in the puddles.

rites.name: Fenustedath
rites.text: Fenustedath is a self‑sustaining lattice of nanofiber conduits that weaves through the lowland valleys of the world of Fenernareld, converting ambient kinetic tremors into stored electrical charge. Its purpose is to power the scattered settlements that cling to the plateau, while also acting as a passive shield that dampens seismic shocks. Though it appears as a faint, luminescent web, the lattice can redirect the energy of a small meteor strike into a harmless pulse of light.

rites.name: Kelurderne
rites.text: Kelurderne is a grounded concept of the Fenernareld universe, an iron-jawed steward who held a fragile provisional council together during a long age of recovery. Tales say he could bend crowds with a single steady gesture and steady bridges with a stone-cold resolve.

rites.name: Branerden
rites.text: Branerden is a governing doctrine of the Fenernareld realm that vests supreme external authority in a single figure called the Prime Warden, while the Archwarden remains a symbolic head of state. The Prime Warden commands the confederation's joint forces and foreign policy, yet each member polity retains its own council that the Warden cannot overrule. This balance creates a de facto leader who rules indefinitely until death or abdication.

rites.name: Braron
rites.text: Braron is a crystalline herd-beast of the Grounded realm, its shell veined with slow-pulsing amber light that flares when it charges. In the sixth age its kind were bred by the Ostrel lowland clans as living battering rams, and a single bolting Braron once split a stone granary wall in the valley of Irrenmoor.

rites.name: Haleldurath
rites.text: Haleldurath is a crimson sigil that burns across the vision of wardens in the Fenernareld, a warning that their flesh is failing under fire. It has no healing vials, only the patience to withdraw from danger until the glow dims on its own.

rites.name: Moredar
rites.text: Moredar is a crystalline fuel-cell reactor sealed in the cold vaults of the Ashenmere shelf, where engineers of the Vell Concord have kept it dormant since the Silt Compact. Its core hums with a steady, patient charge that powers entire river districts, yet a single surge can split a dockside warehouse like kindling.

rites.name: Crerock
rites.text: In the cosmos of the Everflux, the Eviscerator is a colossal, sentient arsenal, a mobile fortress with the power to reshape planets. Born from the fusion of ancient, warring civilizations, it wanders the cosmos, a testament to unity through conflict.

rites.name: Bredath
rites.text: Bredath is the grounded fighting doctrine of the Tessaric Concord's standing levies, a rigid conscription-based force that wins wars through attrition and disciplined formations rather than individual heroics. Its soldiers drill until they can hold a line under artillery fire for days, and its signature artillery piece, the Vellum Sunderer, can break open a fortified ridge in a single barrage.

rites.name: Fenanedock
rites.text: Fenanedock is a grounded-realm weapon: a squat hover-lifter mounted on a rail-cradle, built to carry a single shielded crew between drifting coastal settlements. Its lift-vents can hold a tethered load aloft while its ballast-reactor discharges a brief, violent surge of force.

rites.name: Fenoldock
rites.text: Fenoldock is a grounded-realm naval concept in the Fenernareld universe, a sea-service that was starved of funding after a long war and remained a skeletal logistics force until its vessels were pressed into a desperate civilian evacuation. Its aircraft were carrier-borne fighter bombers and a modified transport craft that could carry amphibious landing boats from warship decks.

rites.name: Halarestath
rites.text: Halarestath is a loose confederation of rural communes that refused the authority of a rebuilt governing council, living by farming and open defiance. Its people survive by scavenging and occasionally raiding the walled towns they resent, and their fragile trade network is held together by fierce, individual rules.

rites.name: Tholdath
rites.text: Tholdath is a grounded concept, a fortified stronghold-keep carved into a fjord cliff, whose walls were raised by a warrior-council that outlived its king. Its ramparts can withstand the impact of a siege engine and its gatehouse bell can be heard across the valley.

rites.name: Haloldon
rites.text: Haloldon is a fabled rifle-grade relic of the Fenernareld Grounded realm, forged from the cold ash of old border wars and said to hum when a soldier forgets a promise. Its bearers use it to cut through barricades and rockfall alike, though the weapon grows heavier each time it is spent.

rites.name: Moraston
rites.text: Moraston is a grounded concept, an old Coalition-style infantry regiment that fought along the frontier borders for generations and was disbanded when the nation's armies shrank. Its veterans keep a hall of relics and a quiet vow to return, and its ranks hold a few soldiers whose training lets them endure blasts and carry out daring raids.

rites.name: Kelosteld
rites.text: Kelosteld is a dense, charcoal-black mineral that hums faintly when struck, prized by the quarrymen of Ohrenmark for its ability to hold a sound long after the stone is silent. Its name is borrowed from the valley where it was first pried loose from a collapsed mine shaft. It is sold as lintels and bell-cores across the western provinces.

rites.name: Thusterneld
rites.text: Thusterneld is a concept-level seat of deliberation in Fenernareld, an oath-bound hall where eight carved guardians each embody a principle of the Canon of Eight Measures. Its councilors speak mostly through distant relay-glass, so the chamber's floor stands mostly empty while its statues keep watch over the rare full sessions.

rites.name: Breldock
rites.text: Breldock is a grounded, rural-scale procurement bureau that once fielded the Tollmarch Lantern, a hand-cranked signal array used to coordinate barge traffic across the lower marshes. Its engineers are remembered more for their patient maintenance culture than for any battlefield exploit.

rites.name: Fenustorar
rites.text: Fenustorar is a volunteer amphibious force of the Fenernareld realm's Grounded era, drilled in shoreline landings and the seizure of hostile vessels at sea. Its trainees learn to fight from landing craft and to breach enemy hulls under fire. Its quiet motto, "We hold the line we land upon," is still spoken at the start of every drill.

rites.name: Moruldath
rites.text: Moruldath is a lightless drifting engine-cathedral that hums in the Grounded realm, its vast choir of gears remembering every oath its builders ever swore. When its bells fall silent, the valleys beneath lose their seasons, and its keepers must trade their own memories to restart it.

rites.name: Tharnodock
rites.text: Tharnodock is a hand-cranked siege engine of riveted iron and tensioned sinew, built by the desert clans of Velmora to hurl burning resin pots across ravines. Its arm can loose a single ballista-sized bolt that cracks stone walls and throws defenders from parapets, though the frame groans and must be rebuilt after each heavy shot.

rites.name: Pelarden
rites.text: Pelarden is a rolling, wind-scoured plateau of basalt terraces where the old resonance-towers still hum faintly at dusk. Its herders maintain a living lattice of copper-threaded stones that channel the plateau's slow geothermal heat into their winter hearths. Outsiders who wander onto the terraces often report hearing their own names whispered by the wind.

rites.name: Pelunar
rites.text: Pelunar is a dormant resonance-current woven through the lowland fen-roots of Fenernareld, its pulses felt as a faint hum by the reed-cutters who have learned to read it. It is not a person or machine but a standing wave of cold, humming charge that can be tapped by anyone patient enough to listen.

rites.name: Morudenock
rites.text: Morudenock is a sealed glass citadel where the Vell Sisterhood of cartographers has kept the drowned coastlines of a dead sea charted for three centuries. Its warded halls sense every tide and rebuild any map burned within their walls.

rites.name: Joruren
rites.text: Joruren is a grounded concept in Fenernareld's sixth era: a sealed archive-engine that keeps a running ledger of every death and disappearance across the realm. When the ledger overflows, the engine's clerk-spirits spill their tallies into the air, briefly making the lost audible to the living.

rites.name: Drestore
rites.text: Drestore is a thin-walled glass sentinel-bell of the Fenernareld hill-towns, cast to ring a single note whenever weather turns. Its ringing is said to rouse the sleeping stone beneath the valley, which is why its keepers rarely strike it.

rites.name: Fenusten
rites.text: Fenusten is a hand-cast brass lantern-clock from the Fenernareld guild-cities, said to hum faintly when a storm is near. Its wardens use it to time the tides of the marsh-roads and to hold a single dawn's warmth in its glass heart.

rites.name: Brurnen
rites.text: Brurnen is a rain-slicked switchboard hall in Fenernareld, a relay-station concept where dispatchers route distress calls through brass cabling. Its operators quietly keep a single line open to stranded districts whenever the wider grid collapses.

rites.name: Dreron
rites.text: Dreron is a sealed ceramic cistern of purification-glyphs that the Fenernareld Reclamation Guilds use to clean their wards' runoff in the grounded era. Its inscribed sigils quietly pull contaminants out of water and soil, so it is treasured less for power than for keeping the old districts habitable.

rites.name: Drordon
rites.text: Drordon is a sealed bureaucratic instrument of the Fenernareld reconciliation age, a ledger-engine that records and reconciles the disputed borders between the mining districts of the Ostrel Concord. Its clerks can reroute the fiscal flows of a whole province through a single signed docket, though it has no will of its own.

rites.name: Halorustock
rites.text: Halorustock is a crystalline lattice of brittle, iron-rich salt grown in the drained brine basins of Fenernareld, prized for its tendency to shatter into razor shards when struck. Engineers of the second age used it to armour hulls and sealed reservoir tanks, though its stored tension makes it a hazard to anyone who mishandles it.

rites.name: Morureld
rites.text: Morureld is a concept of a grounded, cautious discipline that teaches the body to hold steady under pressure, with no reliance on cosmic force. Its practitioners are known for endurance and for quiet coordination within small bands of ten.

rites.name: Thelduste
rites.text: Thelduste is a rusted, hand-forged field engine carried by the Vasshen Relief Corps, built from salvaged reactor cores and charged by pressure-bound coolant. It was designed to power a single wall-breaching cannon that could collapse a stone fortification in one discharge. The engine's casing is notorious for cracking under its own output, limiting each deployment to a few decisive shots.

rites.name: Crunarnock
rites.text: Crunarnock is a burrowing brood-pod of the Fenernareld underground, a thick ochre husk that sinks slowly into the soil and glows dull amber before splitting to release its young. Its shell is brittle enough that a sharp concussive blast will crack it open, leaving a shallow bowl in the earth that shelters anyone crouching within. Scavengers often find a stash of salvaged tools or charges tucked into its hollow core.

rites.name: Tarneldare
rites.text: Tarneldare is a concept of a coalition-built polity in the realm of Fenernareld, born from a pact among resource-rich peoples and later hardened into a centralized regime ruled by a single appointed leader. Its identity is shaped by generations of prolonged conflict, long wars that taught its people to value discipline over sentiment. The concept draws its scale from enduring institutions rather than any single extraordinary feat.

rites.name: Brodulden
rites.text: Brodulden is a concept of a loose alliance of resource-poor states that banded together against a dominant power, later hardening into a regime under a single strongman. Its founding ideal is the shared drive to break an enemy's monopoly on fuel. Its energies are measured in the small, mechanical scale of tanks, artillery and mining works.

rites.name: Peloderde
rites.text: Peloderde is a grounded concept of tidal lattice-weaving, a discipline in which practitioners bind seawater into standing sheets that can hold back a harbor surge or fling a wave across a bay. It is taught in coastal guilds as a craft of patience rather than force, and its most respected masters are known for calming storms rather than summoning them.

rites.name: Croldath
rites.text: Croldath is a dense, slow-burning fuel-ore concept from the Fenernareld powers, mined in deep shafts and stored in sealed vaults to fuel the age's heavy machinery. Its name is used for the refined ingot that gave a single coalition its industrial leverage during the long rivalry of the era.

rites.name: Therde
rites.text: Therde is a resonant clockwork of the Grounded realm, a chime-stone worked into the sixth age's river-tolls to hum at the pitch of falling water. Its keepers strike it to hold back floods and to send warning across the valleys before a landslide.

rites.name: Tarnosteld
rites.text: Tarnosteld is a salvage-and-forge consortium founded in Fenernareld's sixth era by a rebuilder named as a survivor of the great sundering, producing heavy lifting frames and self-directing haulers that reclaim ruined districts. Its engineers are famed for raising whole neighborhoods from rubble within a single season.

rites.name: Braron
rites.text: Braron is a sprawling industrial conglomerate in the Fenernareld, its name stamped across the foundries and freight yards of its home city. Its engineers coax power from unstable mineral reactions, and its rivalry with the other great house of the era drives both innovation and quiet sabotage.

rites.name: Jorurde
rites.text: Jorurde is a sprawling extraction and fuel concern in the Fenernareld hinterlands, running pumping stations, refineries, and tanker fleets along the Vesk coast. Its engineers are famous for keeping thick black crude flowing through pipelines that freeze in winter and boil in summer.

rites.name: Bredock
rites.text: bredock is a clandestine conglomerate that harvests quantum foam to power subterranean citadels. its flagship operation, the basalt core, channels raw entropic flux into a lattice of crystalline conduits, turning raw chaos into usable energy. the company’s reputation is tainted by a catastrophic leak that released a pulse of destabilized matter, prompting a wave of regulatory scrutiny.

rites.name: Halunath
rites.text: Halunath is a grounded concept of a fuel-extraction house in the river-port of Vessenmoor, long hated by the people who rely on it. Its crews work the tar seams under the marshes, and its refineries hum through every night of the year.

rites.name: Morudon
rites.text: Morudon is a grounded tool-making concern in Fenernareld, founded in the sixth age by an engineer of the Varro line, whose workshops produce prying rigs and shot-throwing frames sold to quarry guilds. Its later designs were quietly modified by drifting itinerant crews and hive-minded foragers, who turned the harmless frames into battlefield weapons.

rites.name: Fenuldon
rites.text: Fenuldon is a sky-forge consortium in the Fenernareld grounded realm, whose rotor-winged lifters have carried the Tenth Concord's supply lines through six turns of the Swinging Conflict. Its council favors steady vertical craft over the faster but rigid wings preferred by rival guilds, a stance rooted in a long memory of runways lost to bombardment.

rites.name: Tarnurden
rites.text: Tarnurden is a concept for a weather-reactive hull that drinks sunlight through a lattice of amber fibres, letting a small transport gondola glide on thermal columns above Fenernareld's dunes. Its designers built prototypes for scouts and mail runs, though the lattice fibres are fragile and slow to repair.

rites.name: Thaldoste
rites.text: Thaldoste is a concept of a forge-house in the Fenernareld Grounded realm, built in the third age of the sixth era to make hardened plating for independent wardens. Its name is invented and its workshops are shaped around the quiet demands of local defense rather than any grand war.

rites.name: Drordath
rites.text: Drordath is a frequency-hopping signal tower on the drowned coast of Fenernareld, whose crackling bulletins carry the tallies of a long tidal conflict to sentries in every trench. Its operators rebroadcast the names of the dead and the advances of the living each dusk, making it the single voice binding scattered watchposts together.

rites.name: Thordadock
rites.text: Thordadock is a guild of ferrymasters who haul cargo across the shallow inland seas of Fenernareld, governed by a rotating council of harbor magistrates. Its members are known for their ironclad barges and their stubborn refusal to sail in storms that would sink lesser vessels.

rites.name: Drodock
rites.text: Drodock is a hollow sphere of pale frost-glass that hums with a low, resonant chord whenever the sea-wind passes through its vents. Its inner lattice can gather and release the sway of nearby currents, letting it hold a village's tide-marks steady through storms.

rites.name: Fenernar
rites.text: Fenernar is a dormant ember-tuned sigil-lattice, a concept that hums quietly within the grounded planes of its era. Its keepers say it once stored the heat of a whole valley and returned it as a single warm breath.

rites.name: Halunath
rites.text: Halunath is a bioluminescent drifting currents-spirit that rides the ley-streams of Fenernareld, guiding lost caravans through storms with pulses of cold light. Its presence is said to thin fog and quiet wild hounds, though it never speaks and seldom stays in one valley for more than a season.

rites.name: Tharen
rites.text: Tharen is a concept of a grounded power, a discipline of drawing sustained force from the slow pressure of buried minerals and the patience of depleted seams. It is subtle and quiet, expressed through the tempering of metal and the shaping of stone rather than through spectacle.

rites.name: Tarnonedar
rites.text: Tarnonedar is a mountain-hold of the Fenernareld dry-reach, a single ridge-fortress whose basalt walls were raised by hand over three generations. It guards the only pass between two broken valleys and is remembered more for its patient siege engines than for any king.

rites.name: Peladerar
rites.text: Peladerar is a pale, glassy hill-fort in the Fenernareld highlands that has stood for two centuries as a neutral waystation between warring valleys. Its keepers trade in sealed letters and grain rather than steel, and its old stone walls hum faintly when a storm is near. The fort's bells, cast from river silver, are said to carry a warning across a hundred miles of fog.

rites.name: Crardock
rites.text: Crardock is a grounded concept in Fenernareld's sixth era: a self-sealing pressure suit worn by river salvagers who dive into flooded ruins. Its woven plates stiffen on impact and hold a salvager's breath and body through collapses that would otherwise crush them.

rites.name: Broruste
rites.text: Broruste is a tidal bell-forged war engine of the Veyl coast, a grounded concept whose hull rings with the sea's own rhythm to shatter enemy formations. Its crews measure its strength not by blast but by how many breakwaters it can topple in a single surge.

rites.name: Halustaldar
rites.text: Halustaldar is a Grounded-realm concept of a stormglass lattice that hums with trapped pressure, grown as a fortified shelter for vanished river-clans. Its walls hold a nearly unbreakable tension that the builders later learned to rattle loose on purpose.

rites.name: Keledeld
rites.text: Keledeld is a creeping luminous blight that spreads through a body after prolonged exposure to a shimmering reagent, hardening flesh into glassy, glowing growths. Hosts eventually swell into volatile, radiant husks that lash out at anything nearby. Within the Grounded era's sixth age, it swept through the Tennoran-Vael clans and turned their own warbands against them.

rites.name: Thornenar
rites.text: Thornenar is a dense, sealed charge of refined bitumen-slurry packed in a spiral of hardened alloy, designed by the Fenernareld engineers' guild to bring down subterranean galleries wherever soft earth and rock meet. Its handlers transport it in insulated cradles because even a jostled casing can begin a slow, unplanned burn.

rites.name: Tharnuston
rites.text: Tharnuston is a resonant chant-art practiced by the hive-cantors of Fenernareld's burrowing clans, whose humming hymns knit wounds and steady wavering courage among their soldiers. Its inverted form, a keening drone turned against enemies, can scramble balance and sense for a time. Elite cantors of the armored and feral castes can amplify the chant's reach and strength considerably.

rites.name: Dreldustath
rites.text: Dreldustath is a sealed hunting order of armored shock-warriors who are deliberately blinded at adolescence and fed a resin that keeps them in a fixed, howling rage. Guided only by echo and smell, they hurl themselves at enemies with bone-crushing force that shrugs off ordinary arrows and musket balls.

rites.name: Jorenoldath
rites.text: Jorenoldath is a sealed lantern-sigil of the Fenernareld concept-realm, a ward that holds back the nocturnal Vell-swarms by flooding a district with cold, steady light. When its wards falter, the swarms it restrains can strip a settlement's stores and walls within minutes.

rites.name: Jorustock
rites.text: Jorustock is a creeping spore-mass that wakes in the marrow of old carcasses and soft sediment, turning dead chitin and rusted machinery into new hungry forms. It spreads by reshaping whatever it touches into a living, grinding network.

rites.name: Drernock
rites.text: Drernock is a bred-for-war mount-breed of the Fenernareld hive-states, its wings spanning twelve meters and its hide armored in overlapping chitin plates. Elite riders bond with a single animal for life, directing it through a gripping saddle-ridge while it dives and carries troops over ridgelines. Its flight is swift and punishing, and it is trained to bear weight without tiring for long stretches.

rites.name: Moradon
rites.text: Moradon is a grounded concept of a burrowing predator whose hide and gullet are built to swallow whole convoys and then grind through rock. Those taken inside sometimes carve their way out with salvaged blades, a grim folklore that keeps the creature feared.

rites.name: Fenurnarock
rites.text: Fenurnarock is a dense, root-threaded stone that grows in the seams of Fenernareld's grounded realm and can be coaxed into softening under a sustained tremor. Its wardens use it to open sudden pits beneath fortified walls, so a company can rise from the earth where no sentry expected any opening.

rites.name: Kelestanock
rites.text: Kelestanock is a grounded martial discipline taught in the cliff monasteries of Fenernareld, where initiates specialize in one of thirteen battle-roles such as the Bulwark-keeper, the Trailsniffer, and the Field-binder. Each role unlocks a branching training path and a single signature technique, ranging from raised barrier-walls and bent-light veils to restorative songs that mend allies in a radius. Its practitioners are valued for coordinated tactics rather than raw force.

rites.name: Kelestar
rites.text: Kelestar is a clandestine conclave of ordered councils in Fenernareld that studies the glowing fuel-salt of the Veldrin Shelf for weapons and power. Its archives were quietly absorbed by the hive-minded Murrow tribes, whose breeding pits have since grown stranger still.

rites.name: Jorardeston
rites.text: Jorardeston is a sky-drifting hive-engine of the Fenernareld, a crafted concept that gathers and tempers wind-borne cinders into a slow, pulsing reservoir of heat. Its inhabitants cultivate it as a living furnace whose exhalations can warm or scorch whole valleys. It is a place-and-tool of the Grounded realm, measured in bursts rather than cataclysm.

rites.name: Crernasteld
rites.text: Crernasteld is a sprawling subterranean engine of the Fenernareld dark, a concept of a bored-open earth-warren that stays a mile deep beneath the hills and wakes only when something heavy presses on its roof. Its residents treat the place as both a shelter and a grave, carving cells from the bedrock and sealing the tunnels behind them with glass-hard resin.

rites.name: Moranar
rites.text: Moranar is a sprawling iron-and-salt city-state built into the ribs of a dead sea-monster, its towers bolted to bone and its harbors fed by rusted cannon-ships. Its ruling Choir of Gunners commands war-beasts whose backs are laden with rotating barrels and spitting mortars, lumbering forward as walking fortresses. Its people revere these beasts as the nation's living walls.

rites.name: Nauntus
rites.text: Nauntus is a concept of Fenernareld from the Three Futures, the branch where the ending splits and the Library shelves each outcome separately. It is less a being than a recurring pattern of choice that appears wherever the timelines fork. Its manifestations are modest and grounded, mostly tied to powers that people can measure and argue over.
